name: Spot Price Directly Used as Pricing Basis
code_features: Function uses pair.getReserves() or balanceOf result directly in asset pricing
No TWAP or other time-weighted mechanism applied

name: Short-Window / Manipulatable TWAP
code_features: Uses AMM TWAP with sampling window too short (e.g., 1-2 blocks)
Can be manipulated by flash loans or consecutive trades

name: Centralized / Unverified Price Feed
code_features: Relies on a single off-chain API feed without decentralized verification
Multi-source aggregation lacks deviation outlier filtering
Single admin can update on-chain price

name: Stale Oracle Data
code_features: Does not check updatedAt, roundId or equivalent freshness fields
May use outdated, manipulatable historical prices

name: Oracle Update Heartbeat / Delay Tolerance Missing
code_features: Does not check the time since the last price update
Relies on a heartbeat mechanism without verifying if the price is stale
Allows prolonged delay before price refresh

name: Mint/Burn Price Depends on Instant Reserves
code_features: Mint or burn function calculates share/token amount using current reserve0, reserve1 directly
No slippage protection or delay mechanism

name: Collateral/Margin Ratio Uses Manipulatable Price
code_features: Lending or leverage protocol calculates collateralFactor, healthFactor or margin requirements using easily manipulatable price source (e.g., AMM spot)
Could trigger unfair liquidations

name: TVL/Volume-Driven Fee or Reward Distribution
code_features: Fee allocation or reward distribution depends on totalSupply, totalValueLocked, or similar instantaneously modifiable state variables

name: Missing Deadline / Protection Window
code_features: Swap/deposit/withdraw functions lack a deadline parameter or set it too long
Predictable periodic operations (e.g., rebalancing) lack a protection window

name: No Slippage Protection / Excessive Tolerance
code_features: amountOutMin is set to 0 or left entirely to user discretion without contract-enforced maximum slippage

name: State Changed Multiple Times in One Transaction (Reentrancy-Type Price Manipulation)
code_features: Price or reserve updates happen after an external call (e.g., swap callback) and no reentrancy guard is used

name: Oracle Address Update Without Timelock/Multi-sig
code_features: Function updating oracle address is callable only by owner without timelock or multi-signature verification

name: Economic Parameters Adjustable by Privileged Role
code_features: Fee rate, interest rate, collateral ratio etc. can be changed by a single admin account without timelock

name: Concentrated Token Mint/Burn Privileges
code_features: An address with mint/burn privileges can arbitrarily inflate or deflate the token supply, affecting price

name: Exploitable Rounding Direction
code_features: Division or modulo operations do not handle remainders correctly; attackers can repeatedly extract tiny dust amounts

name: Decimal Mismatch in Price Calculation
code_features: Price or exchange rate calculation mixes tokens with different decimals (e.g., USDC 6 decimals vs ETH 18 decimals) without normalization

name: AMM Curve / Parameter Misconfiguration
code_features: Custom curve parameters allow unreasonable slippage during extreme trades; or standard constant-product AMM lacks protection for extreme volumes, leading to severe price deviation

name: Reliance on External Protocol / Bridge as Sole Price Source
code_features: Core logic (liquidation, borrowing) directly calls getAmountOut on an external DEX or cross-chain bridge without a fallback price source or circuit breaker

name: Unverified Assumption of External LP Token Value
code_features: Protocol accepts LP tokens as collateral and values them at their 'current rate' without verifying that the underlying composition hasn't been manipulated

name: Cross-Protocol Call Without Return/Consistency Check
code_features: External swap/liquidate calls do not verify return values, or inconsistent state may result from a revert in the called contract

name: Unverified Cross-Protocol Price Dependency
code_features: Protocol B's liquidation or pricing logic depends on liquidity or price from Protocol A without validation
Manipulating Protocol A's state indirectly distorts Protocol B's price feed
